title: The nonpositive scalar-periodic cochain complex
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a sheaf $M$ and a square-zero endomorphism $f:M\to M$, define $X_M^i=M$ for $i\leq0$ and $X_M^i=0$ for $i>0$. Define $d_f^i:X_M^i\to X_M^{i+1}$ as $f$ for $i<0$, using these term identifications, and zero otherwise. The cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with these terms and differentials is the nonpositive periodic complex of $f$; its term identification in degree $i\leq0$ is the identity identification $X_M^i\cong M$. In particular, for a restriction-compatible family $t=(t_U)_U$ with $t_U^2=0$, let $\mu_t:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O$ be sectionwise multiplication $a\mapsto t_Ua$. The scalar-periodic complex $P(t)$ is the above complex for $M=\mathcal O$ and $f=\mu_t$. The equations $\mu_t^2=0$ and $d_f^{i+1}d_f^i=0$ supply the complex compatibility proofs. No kernel-image equality or exactness assumption is part of this definition.
